newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr support at 111.45 yen seen crucial.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr support at 111.45 yen seen crucial.

text.p: Solid support at 111.45 yen on Friday could provide a springboard for the dollar to mount another attack on 112.10 yen near term, according to chartists.
The dollar soared briefly on Wednesday to 112.10 yen, a 32- month high.
"As long as the market maintains that support, I think there's a chance we could retest the 112.10 area," said Joseph Klettner, a foreign exchange technical analyst at Chase Securities Inc.
Klettner sketched the dollar's short-term range between 111.45 and 112.10 yen.
Should the dollar move out of its present range with a move below 111.09 yen, he warned, that would be a first indication the dollar probably put in a top this week at 112.10.
"Then, I think, we could head back down to the last significant pivot point 108.86," said Klettner, adding that level is an important low from two weeks ago.
The dollar had seesawed after news that U.S. non-farm payrolls fell 40,000 in September, while average hourly earnings rose to $11.92 in September from $11.86 in August.
In afternoon dealings, the dollar traded around 111.76 yen, up modestly from 111.55/60 yen at the opening.
I.D.E.A. Inc technical strategist Ben Morden deemed a dollar close above 111.19 yen, a previous high from July 8, a bullish signal.

"I think that's a bullish signal that maybe we can continue to hold these levels and push for 113.58, the high from January 1994," Morden said. As for when the dollar might attempt a rally to 113.58 yen, he said it could be possible in two to four weeks.

On a cautionary note, he said, "There are some overbought selling signs and ... the fact that mark/yen is struggling to really do anything above 73 is a little bit of a negative sign (for dollar/yen), but I would stay with the trend next week."
The German currency traded near 72.96 yen in the afternoon on Friday. The dollar stood higher against the German unit, trading near 1.5320 marks, up from 1.5305/10 at the opening.
Morden contends the dollar could test next week 1.54 marks, an area of chart congestion.
He mentioned a number of positive factors for the dollar, including the fact that some longer term studies turned positive when the dollar broke above the 1.53 marks area a few days ago.
